Short answer: yes, very likely a floating DTSTART / missing TZID in the ics.

What likely happened:
- Marissa's calendar client generated an event using a local timezone reference (PT) but the exported ics used a floating DTSTART or omitted a VTIMEZONE block.
- When that file is forwarded/imported into Google Calendar (or when internal mail forwarding strips metadata), some clients interpret a floating DTSTART as "take these wall-clock numbers and apply the recipient's calendar timezone"; others default to UTC. The result: inconsistent local times and DST surprises.

Fixes:
1) Create the event using an explicit TZID in the DTSTART or include a full VTIMEZONE definition in the ics.
2) Safer: generate invites with UTC DTSTART (e.g., DTSTART:20270721T160000Z for 9:00 PT) — UTC is unambiguous.
3) As a user-level workaround, include the explicit wall-clock conversions in the description and the invite title (e.g., "9:00 AM PT / 5:00 PM BST / 02:00 AEST") and a short note: "If your calendar shows a different time after forwarding, please follow the UTC time: 2027-07-21T16:00:00Z".

I'll re-generate a UTC-based ics and attach. Also recommend sending the invite from our primary org account (no third-party forwards) so Google doesn't drop the VTIMEZONE block.

—Rishi
